evidence: Greenbank (6) and the misspelled Tiger of Canada West (1) are William Hugh Graham's, about 7/22 weighted citations. The Cartwright thesis and article (4) are William Roger Graham's; Siam is Walter Armstrong Graham's. Several further titles belong to other Grahams or are incomplete.

Deportation Nation (22) is catalogued under Kanstroom, Dan, with the statement of responsibility Daniel Kanstroom. The deportation, social control and punishment article (1) is also Daniel Kanstroom's. Dan and Daniel identify the same author.

A Sabinada (9) is Paulo César de Souza's; the Círculo do Livro fragment may add one, giving approximately 10/23. Emprego, salários e pobreza (2) and Determinação dos Salários (1) are Paulo Renato's. The forestry works are Paulo Ferreira's; the Portuguese health-system article is Paulino Artur Ferreira de Sousa's.

Ethics and its Portuguese and French translations, the political and theological-political treatises, correspondence and collected selections are all the philosopher's works. Baruch and Benedictus are alternative forms of his name; the Theologico-Philosophicus title appears to be a bibliographic error.

Conflict and Crisis (6), Tumultuous Years (4), Unsilent Revolution (2), and the other American political titles belong to Robert J. Donovan, approximately 15/27 weighted citations. No Popery (4), Military Origins (3), and the British religious-history titles belong to Robert Kent Donovan. This substantial mixture falls below the specified mostly threshold; distinct-thesis overlap is unavailable.

The author's university publication list includes Frankish Rural Settlement (11), Crusader Castles (5), Collapse of the Eastern Mediterranean (5), and the settlement and borders studies. Ronnie Ellenblum also coauthored the Tell Ateret earthquake article. Roni and Ronnie refer to this same scholar.

Taxation and Governmental Finance (10), the editions of 1587 (10), Ming fiscal administration and reign studies, and the military and bureaucratic articles are Ray Huang's. The library record explicitly associates the English byline Ray Huang with the author heading Huang Renyu (黄仁宇).

O corpo de Deus (8), O pináculo (1), the Cidadão/concept-history entries (4), and Irmandades (1) are Beatriz Catão Cruz Santos's: approximately 14/22, close to two thirds. The curriculum (4) and uniforms (1) works are Beatriz Boclin Marques dos Santos's; Entre Mouros (2) and Memórias do Ultramar (1) are Beatriz Carvalho dos Santos's.

As múltiplas faces da escravidão (8), Jogos de interesses (4 plus variant entries), and the Minas slavery, wealth and client-network studies are Carlos Leonardo Kelmer Mathias's. Notas para uma História do Judiciário (2) is explicitly credited by FUNAG to Carlos Fernando Mathias. Estimated LC share is 28/30; the journal-only fragment is less certain.

Dicionário de História de São Paulo (6), História dos velhos teatros (5), Departamento do Arquivo (1), and O bairro de Pinheiros (1) are Antônio Barreto do Amaral's; the 1972 journal fragment likely adds one, roughly 14/21. The historical-concepts dictionary is Amaral Azevedo's, O Sentido da Educação is Azevedo Amaral's, and the military Indicador is Antônio José do Amaral's. The painting text is Antônio Henrique Amaral's (1995, cited in a 2015 article); newspaper fragments remain unresolved.
